title: Munich Agreement
summary: Leaders of Germany, Britain, France and Italy met in Munich and reached a settlement permitting German annexation of the Sudetenland in western Czechoslovakia. Czechoslovakia was not consulted. Intended as appeasement to avert war, it became a byword for the futility of appeasing expansionist states.

importance.justification: Emblematic act of appeasement that dismembered Czechoslovakia on the eve of World War II.

sources.title: Munich Agreement | Definition, Summary, & Significance | Britannica

reviewer_note: Sources agree on 30 September 1938 as the signing date; the conference ran 29-30 September (World History Encyclopedia) and the meeting began on 29 September (Britannica). The second source text is truncated.  Britannica says Chamberlain met Hitler at Godesberg on 22 September; World History says 22 September too, but gives 15 September for Berchtesgaden visit while Britannica says mid-September.  Place coordinates are approximate.} (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from Encyclopaedia Britannica, World History Encyclopedia; quotes machine-checked.)
